summary_en: KAGA ELECTRONICS raised its FY2027 full-year dividend forecast to 180 yen per share from 160 yen, comprising 140 yen ordinary dividend and 40 yen special dividend, reflecting upward revision of net profit guidance driven by strong semiconductor demand.
title_en: Announcement Regarding Revision of Full-Year Earnings Forecast for Fiscal Year Ending March 2027 (Upward Revision) and Revision of Dividend Forecast (Increase in Dividend)
translation_en_brief:
KAGA ELECTRONICS announced an increase in its dividend forecast for fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. The company raised the annual dividend per share from the previously projected 160 yen to 180 yen, comprising 140 yen as ordinary dividend and 40 yen as special dividend. The interim dividend remains at 100 yen per share, which includes 70 yen ordinary and 30 yen special dividend.

The dividend hike reflects the company's upward revision of earnings guidance. The company increased its full-year net profit attributable to parent company shareholders from 29.0 billion yen to 32.0 billion yen, or 671.28 yen per share from 608.35 yen. This revision was driven by stronger-than-expected performance in the electronic components business amid sustained semiconductor demand centered on AI-related applications, rising prices, and increased spot sales of supply-constrained semiconductors.

Based on the revised guidance adjusted for 7.0 billion yen in non-cash gains from negative goodwill related to the consolidation of Shinko Shoji K.K., the company expects a consolidated dividend payout ratio of 34.3 percent and dividend on equity (DOE) of 5.3 percent, both within the targets set in the Medium-Term Management Plan 2027 (consolidated dividend payout ratio of 30–40 percent and DOE of 4.0 percent or higher).
